Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (K.C.S.E)
 FORM FOUR
 311/2
 HISTORY AND GOVERNMENT
 PAPER 2
 INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATE
 1. Write your name and index number in the spaces provided.
 2. Sign and write the date of examination in the spaces provided.
 3. This paper consists of section A, B and C.
 4. Answer ALL questions in section A any three in section B and any two questions in
 section C.
 5.All questions must be answered in English.
 SECTION A
 Marking scheme
 1. Identify the main method used by anthropologists to obtain information on
 history and government (1mark)
 • Observation (1x1=1marks)
 2. Give evidence that shows the early man developed religious practices during the
 late Stone Age period (1mark)
 • They buried their dead with their belonging. (1x1=1marks)
 3. State two theories that explain the origin and spread of agriculture (2marks)
 i. diffusion theory one area theory / centrifugal
 ii. independent theory (2x1=2marks)
 4. Name two participants of the Trans-Saharan trade (2 marks)
 i. Tuaregs
 ii. Takshifs
 iii. Berbers (2x1=2marks)
 5. State the main advantages of using a cellphone as a means of communication
 (1mark)
 • It is mobile / carried anywhere. (1x1=1mark)
 6. Name two symbols of authority in the Buganda kingdom in the pre- colonial
 period (2marks)
 i. Royal spear
 ii. royal drum
 iii. Throne
 iv. Royal tombs (2x1=2marks)
 7. State two factors that led to the decline of Meroe as an early urban center in
 Africa (2marks)
 i. The rise of the Axum Kingdom which developed East of Meroe
 ii. King of Axum subdued and destroyed Meroe in 350A.D
 iii.
 Desertification due to deforestation led to decline of food supply for her
 people
 iv. Exhaustion of iron ore (2x1=2marks)
 8. Name two communities that took part in the maji maji uprising of 1905-1907 in
 Tanganyika (2marks)
 i. Ngindo
 ii. Matumbi
 iii. Pogoro
 iv. Ngoni
 v. Mpunga/mbunga
 vi. Luguru
 vii. Zaramo
 viii. Bena
 ix. Ndendeule
 x. Wamwera (2x1=2marks)
 9. State two social factors that led to the scramble for colonies in Africa (2marks)
 i. The need to abolish slave trade
 ii. Desire to spread Christianity / to protect missionaries
 iii. Desire to spread in civilization / education
 iv. Need to settle surplus population (2x1=2marks)
 10. Give one system of administration used by the British colonial Government
 (1mark)
 i. Direct system of ruling
 ii. Indirect system of ruling. (1x1=1mark)
 11. Identify the underground movement formed in South Africa after the banning of
 African national congress party (ANC) (1mark)
 • Umkhonto we Sizwe / spear of the nation. (1x1=1mark)
 12. Identify two communes in Senegal where the policy of assimilation was
 successful (2marks)
 i. Dakar
 ii. St Louis
 iii. Goree
 iv. Rufisque (2x1=2marks)
 13. State the main reason why USA did not take part initially in the First World
 War (1mark)
 • In line with Monroe Doctrine. (1x1=1mark)
 14. Name the organization where the king/queen of England is the head. (1mark)
 • Common wealth. (1x1=1mark)
 15. State the immediate incident that sparked off the Second World War (1mark)
 • German invasion of Poland led by Adolf Hitler. (1x1=1mark)
 16. Name two permanent members of the united nation security council (2marks)
 i. Britain
 ii. U.S.A
 iii. Russia
 iv. France
 v. China (2x1=2marks)
 17. Name the international organization that took over from organization of
 African union. (1mark)
 • African Union (1x1=1mark)
 SECTION B
 18. a) Give 3 dwelling places of man in the Stone Age period (3marks)
 i. Rock Shelters
 ii. Tree trunks
 iii. On trees
 iv. Caves/stone cares
 v. In forest (3x1=3marks)
 (b) Factors that led to Agrarian Revolution in U.S.A
 i. Immigration of people as the result of land enclosure system spread the
 skills and knowledge of Agriculture
 ii. Practice of plantation / large – scale farming due to use of machinery
 iii. Discovery of refrigerator by an American Scientist which preserved
 food at low temperature
 iv. Infrastructure development such as roads, water ways and
 communication networks
 v. Crop zoning as different regions had suitable soils for different crops
 vi. Use of hybrid seeds / Animals cross breeding / selective breeding
 vii. Use of farm machinery e.g. steel plough by John Deere
 viii. Invention of and use of fertilizers
 ix. Use of pesticides to control crop and animal diseases
 x. Discovery of oil and electricity which were used as energy in farms
 and industries for processing agricultural raw materials to finished
 goods.
 (6x2=12marks)
 19. a) Mention 3 continents involved in the Trans- Atlantic trade (3marks)
 i. America
 ii. Africa
 iii. (iii) Europe
 (3x1=3marks)
 (b) Organization of the Transatlantic Trade
 i. It spread between N. Africa the Americas and Europe across the Atlantic
 Ocean.
 ii. The Europeans brought manufactured goods to West Africa and exchanged
 them with slaves
 iii. Salves were sold at particular centers along the Coast of West Africa e.g.
 Lagos, Accra etc
 iv. The slaves were stored in barracoons awaiting transportation to the Americans
 v. Trade goods brought to Africa included cloths, guns, ammunitions, knives,
 enamel bowls, metal bars, spirits, glassware, jewelry , sugar etc
 vi. The main form of transport was water transport. The sailing ships docked in
 prominent ports in West Africa e.g. Lagos, Whyday, Accra etc. from Europe
 there were ports such as Manchester, Liverpool, Glasgow
 vii. The middlemen transported slaves to the ports exchanged with European
 traders at the Coast
 viii. In America, slaves were auctioned to landowners used to work in the
 plantation for production of raw materials to be transported to European
 industries. (6x2=12marks)
 20. (a) Economic reasons why the Europeans acquired colonies in Africa
 i. To obtain cheaper source of raw materials for their industries.
 ii. To search for markets for their manufactured goods
 iii. To acquire areas to invest their surplus capital
 iv. Need to protect European traders and investment in Africa
 v. Need for cheaper labor in production of he required materials after abolition of
 slave trade.
 vi. Availability of pockets of minerals in Africa such as gold, bronze etc.
 (5x1=5marks)
 (b) Reasons why Lewanika collaborated with the British
 i. To protect his kingdom against the Germans and the Portuguese
 ii. Desired W. education and civilization
 iii. He wanted to get protection from internal enemies / safeguard his position
 iv. He was encouraged to collaborate by King Khama of Ngwato who had
 already sought British protection against the Boers
 v. He saw the futility of resisting a strong power like Britain
 vi. He wanted the British to protect his Kingdom from attacks by the Shona and
 Ndebele
 vii. He was influenced by European missionaries who had earlier visited his
 kingdom like Henry Morton Stanley (5x2=10marks)
 21. (a) Reasons why the British used direct role to administer S. Rhodesia
 (Zimbabwe) (3mks)
 i. To have full control of the economy of Zimbabwe through exploiting the
 resources
 ii. To ensure complete control over the African communities to reduce resistance
 iii. To replace existing traditional system of administration of Indunas which had
 been destroyed / disrupted by British occupation of the area?
 iv. Existing of BSAC that supplied enough personnel who occupied admin posts
 v. BSAC had enough money to pay for admin cost
 vi. The Chimurenga war (1896 – 1897) eroded the British confidence in using
 traditional chiefs in the admin of the colony. (3x1=3marks)
 (b) Challenges faced by Nationalists in S. Africa
 i. Harassed / detained /jailed by security agents which demoralized them.
 ii. Political parties / associations were banned thereby denying them their rights
 to associate / assemble
 iii. They were forced into exile as they feared to be persecuted / tortured / death
 iv. The pass laws introduced by the apartheid regime curtailed their movement
 v. The Apartheid regime prescribed / censored publications which denied them
 the right to access information
 vi. Their communities were divided along ethnic lines / Bantustans hence
 hampered formation of a United trial
 vii. Inadequate funds hence couldn’t out activities effectively
 viii. Division among the Nationalist / leadership wrangles.
 (6x2=12marks)
 SECTION C
 22. (a) Weapons used during the first world war (3mks)
 i. Poisonous gas
 ii. Tankers
 iii. Machine guns
 iv. Airplanes / aircrafts
 v. Sub marines. (3x1=3marks)
 (b) Reasons why the league of Nations failed to maintain world peace.
 i. Some aero planes nations opposed the peace treaty of Versailles because it
 favored the allied nations that had fought against German.
 ii. U.S.A did not support the league because it did not want to get involved in
 European affairs
 iii. The membership of the organization was not all that inclusive. Some
 countries were left out while others were not given a chance to join.
 iv. The league violated the objectives of maintaining world peace by supporting
 some nations claim against others.
 v. Members were concerned with their sovereignty as opposed to the interests of
 the league of Nations.
 vi. Some members of the league adopted the policy of appeasement towards
 certain regimes inorder to avoid confrontation thus weakening it.
 vii. Shortage of funds made it difficult for the league to implement its programmes
 viii. The league lacked its own army to implement its decisions where peace was
 threatened
 ix. The search for colonies diverted the members attention from the activities of
 the league of Nations
 x. Rise of dictatorship regimes weakened the league as these dictators refused to
 accept its resolution
 xi. The economic depression of 1929 weakened most of the world economies,
 hence they were not able to support the league financially.
 (6x2=12marks)
 23. (a) characteristics of the commonwealth members states
 i. The use of English as the official language
 ii. They recognize king / queen as the head
 iii. They co-operate in sport / games / exchange information
 iv. They have close economic ties
 v. Most of the states have similar legal / administration system / parliamentary
 system
 vi. They have a common military tradition based on the British one
 vii. They enjoy universal adult suffrage
 viii. Members hold regular conferences of heads of states. (5x1=5marks)
 (b) Challenges facing economic community of west African states (ECOWAS)
 i. Poor transport and communication
 ii. Division between francophone and Anglophone countries
 iii. Political instabilities in member countries e.g. Liberia, Nigeria etc
 iv. National interests outweigh regional issues
 v. ECOWAS members are also members of other organizations
 vi. Ideological differences which leads to mistrust and suspicion
 vii. Members states are still dependent on formed colonial masters / neo-
 colonialism
 viii. Disparities in size, population and wealth that hinder development
 ix. Use of different currencies that keep fluctuating thus hampering trade
 x. Closure of borders making movement of people and services difficult
 xi. A lot of foreign interference
 xii. Influx of workers from less to more developed areas within the member states.
 (5x2=10marks)
 24. (a) Social problems faced by Democratic republic of Congo (DRC) since
 independence
 i. High number of refugees who have freed due to civil wars in their countries
 ii. High poverty caused by unemployment
 iii. High unemployment rates due to high population / rural urban migration
 iv. Inadequate social facilities / infrastructures
 v. Increased crime rates such as theft
 vi. Population pressure due to high birth rate
 vii. Poor developed system of health in the country. (3x1=3marks)
 (b) Political challenges in Africa since independence
 i. Ideological differences created by the world wars
 ii. Lack of experienced leaders at independence who were to take over the
 leadership after colonizers
 iii. Political instability characterized by coup d’états e.g. Nigeria, D.R.C, Somali
 etc.
 iv. Ethnicity / tribalism leading to serious political crises
 v. Neo colonialism as most countries still heavily relies on their former colonial
 masters
 vi. Dictatorial role leading to competition and mismanagement of state resources
 vii. Introduction of multi-partisan democracy leading to political confusion
 viii. Rise of nationalism where national interests conflicts with continental and
 global interests. (6x2=12marks)
